## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run in this search yet. In generation 0, all 84 trials across 7 worlds scored zero, with training success also zero. The agent is not learning at all; the problem is not overfitting to training designs. Changing the architecture family made no difference: priors that assume the action layout and priors that assume none both failed. That points to learning dynamics rather than what the network can represent. One possibility is that the agent quickly settles on choosing DONE, because random placements earn negative reward. Another is that the world behaves differently from the description. Seed noise is unknown. Round 1 tests regions gen 0 never tried: lr 3e-3, n_envs 512, gae_lambda 0.8, a much smaller network, and long-horizon credit (gamma 0.995, lambda 0.99). Two of the candidates also give the critic and DONE logit a direct view of the raw observation. Each proposal says what result would refute it, so even all-zero scores rule out these recipe regions.

### Round 2
There have now been 87 trials across generation 0 and round 1. Every one scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, so the agent is not learning at all. Round 1 ruled out three more fixes: a faster recipe (426k steps, lr 3e-3, gae_lambda 0.8), a tiny network, and long-horizon credit with a direct path from the raw observation to DONE. Because every score is 0, I cannot rank ideas or measure seed noise. Two explanations remain. (a) To earn any exact-build bonus at all, the network has to compute three things: where the brick lands (the highest point under its footprint), whether that layer is missing in the target, and whether the placement would seal empty cells. Generic trunks may not find this in time. (b) Action indices may not line up with grid cells in this world. Two candidates give the head a built-in landing-layer structure made only from learned features, each with a different recipe. The third adds a residual layout remap, initialised at zero, that can learn any action permutation.

### Round 3
All 90 trials so far (generation 0 plus 6 here) scored 0 on both dev and training success. That covers recipe speed, exploration, long-horizon credit, a direct DONE path, small networks, a learned landing-layer head and a learned layout remap. Since every network family fails, including MLPs and dense heads, the cause is probably something they all share. The world may differ from its description. One shared assumption none of the trials has tested is scale: if the inputs are larger than described, default-initialised networks will output huge logits. The policy then becomes nearly deterministic from the start and PPO cannot learn. None of the networks used normalisation or zero-initialised output layers. This round tests that guess in three ways: the starting network with normalisation, a layout-free dense head with normalisation, and the normalised network with full-episode rollouts and large minibatches. If all three still score 0, the input-scale explanation is ruled out.

### Round 4
Every trial so far has scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success in the last 10%. That covers 84 trials in generation 0 and 9 in this search: recipe extremes, tiny networks, a landing-layer head, a layout remap, normalisation with zero-initialised outputs, and a layout-free dense head. With nothing above zero, seed noise can't be measured and no idea can be ranked against another. One explanation I suspect but have not tested: the shaped reward still pays for sloppy placements (for example a 2x2 brick covering 3 target cells and 1 wrong cell). An agent can settle on that local optimum and never get an exact build, so it never sees the +1 bonus. Precision has to come from learning the best immediate placement exactly. With one round left, I'm trying three different angles: a near-greedy, low-entropy, many-sample recipe; shared cell scores across brick types; and a head that sees each footprint cell separately instead of only pooled summaries.
